stories.h: Manchevski's Sister Brother Manhole Cover wins Tokyo's top prize
sum: Milcho Manchevski's North Macedonian social satire Sister Brother Manhole Cover won the top award at the Tokyo International Film Festival on 4 November. It follows two siblings on society's bottom rung who survive by stealing bronze statues and manhole covers; jury president Rolf de Heer praised its mix of humour, tragedy and compassion.

The special jury prize went to Sun Xun's hand-crafted animated feature Magic Atlas, made over more than a decade. Argentina's Lisandro Alonso was named best director for Double Freedom, about a forest woodcutter who must care for his sister, and Hu Ling won best actress.
pts: Top prize: Sister Brother Manhole Cover
Special jury prize: animated Magic Atlas

stories.h: Gugu's World: Brazil's Oscar pick is a colourful queer coming-of-age
sum: Screen Daily calls Allan Deberton's Gugu's World a touching, sweetly appealing drama about an 11-year-old queer boy growing up with his grandmother in Brazil's northeast backlands. Young lead Yuri Gomes is singled out for a poised, natural performance as a promising footballer who loves beads, glitter and bright scarves.

The film blends grief, resilience and self-acceptance, and its pink-and-blue production design mirrors Gugu's riot of colour. It won Berlin's Generation Kplus Crystal Bear, is Brazil's official Oscar submission, and opens in Brazil on 5 November.

stories.h: Wicker tops the UK box office; Pattinson's Primetime opens third
sum: Black Bear scored its first UK-Ireland number one with Wicker, a romantic fantasy starring Olivia Colman as a fisherwoman who asks a basket weaver (Alexander Skarsgård) to make her a husband. It took £1.7m over 30 October to 1 November from 676 cinemas.

A24's Primetime, with Robert Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen, opened third on £1.3m. Ghosts: The Possession of Button House held second, while Laika's Wildwood has reached £2.8m and a BFI 4K restoration of The Devils drew a strong £220,000 from 73 venues.

stories.h: La Bola Negra wins London Film Festival audience award
sum: Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo's La Bola Negra, an exploration of early-20th-century queer culture in Spain starring Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau and Penélope Cruz, won the BFI London Film Festival's audience award for best feature. It earlier premiered in Cannes competition, won TIFF's People's Choice award and is Spain's Oscar submission.

Grace Harper Brighouse's documentary Dependence, about loving an addict told through decades of home movies, was voted best British discovery. London screenings hit record 96% occupancy. La Bola Negra opens in UK-Ireland cinemas on 6 November; Netflix holds US rights.

stories.h: Elsinore and I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning lead Bifa nominations
sum: Simon Stone's Elsinore, about actor Ian Charleson's final run as Hamlet, leads the 2026 British Independent Film Awards with 12 nominations, including best film, best director and best lead for Andrew Scott. Clio Barnard's I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning follows with eight.

Barnard's film, a Cannes Directors' Fortnight winner, follows five Birmingham friends in their 30s amid the housing crisis and is up for best ensemble. Ashley Walters' prison drama Animol, his directing debut, has seven nods including best debut director.
stories.q: I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

stories.h: Kefi: an irreverent, eye-catching Japanese debut about three sisters
sum: Kisin Saito's debut Kefi, premiering in Tokyo's Nippon Cinema Now strand, follows three sisters reuniting in the family home after their estranged father dies. Screen Daily says any likeness to Kore-eda's Our Little Sister ends there: this is wilfully unpredictable, sometimes baffling, and thrillingly alive.

Saito shoots it himself and ditches the grey, under-lit look common in indie cinema for something brighter and bolder. The review predicts it will divide audiences but calls it a loud arrival of a new voice, ideal for anyone tired of soft-focus romances.

stories.h: Letterboxd's November Unreleased Gems: festival hits, rentable for 30 days
sum: Letterboxd's Video Store has a new batch of Unreleased Gems: festival favourites with no distribution yet, available to rent digitally for 30 days only. This month's picks come from Tribeca, Slamdance and SXSW.

The lineup ranges from a raucous comedy about Jackass-style stunt performers to a documentary at the crossroads of fashion and hip-hop, a politically charged thriller about disillusioned youth and a tender film on male friendship. Availability and prices vary by region.

stories.h: Shelf Life: November's best restorations and re-releases
sum: Letterboxd's monthly Shelf Life column rounds up repertory screenings and physical-media releases, built around connections between films and filmmakers. Highlights include a Japanese New Wave master's collected works, David Bowie's most luminous star vehicle and Bong Joon Ho's monster movie.

Also flagged: a 10th-anniversary Train to Busan 4K set, a 35th-anniversary re-release of Zhang Yimou's Raise the Red Lantern, My Sassy Girl at 25 and a new restoration of Edward Yang's That Day, on the Beach.

stories.h: My Chemical Romance finally hit No. 1 with The Black Parade, 20 years late
sum: My Chemical Romance have scored their first-ever No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with The Black Parade, two decades after it first came out and stalled at No. 2. A 20th-anniversary deluxe edition had only re-entered the chart at No. 139 before rocketing to the top of the Nov. 7 chart.

It is the longest wait on record for an album to reach No. 1, and the biggest leap to the summit since Taylor Swift's Fearless re-recording in 2021. MCR knocked Olivia Rodrigo to No. 2; she recently posted about attending one of their shows.
stories.q: My Chemical Romance The Black Parade

stories.h: Eterna's Push drifts from slacker rock into blissed-out post-rock
stories.why: Indie rock with a dreamy turn
sum: Guillem Peeters, the Barcelona-born, London-based musician who drummed on bar italia's Tracey Denim, releases his third Eterna album Push on 6 November. The Line of Best Fit's reviewer admits the first two records failed their personal slacker-rock test, but says this one finally shows real care.

The scrappy home-demo collage has given way to carefully shaped, hazy post-rock expanses, with tracks like "Kyrie" singled out for moments of genuine magic. The verdict: a confident leap from shrugging indie into something richer and more immersive.

stories.h: Mamalarky announce fourth album Hover, share "Sad Songs"
sum: Austin indie rockers Mamalarky are following April 2025's Hex Key quickly: their new album Hover arrives in February on Epitaph. The first taste, "Sad Songs," is a lightly psychedelic pop-rock track that Stereogum calls a gem, with a breakup-weary hook from Livvy Bennett.

Bennett describes it as the feeling of the first sunny day after a long low stretch, meant to keep company with anyone dealing with loneliness or loss. The 12-track album also includes "Sycamore Tree," "Mirage" and "Sweet Tooth."
pts: Hover out in February on Epitaph

stories.h: Oso Oso's Jade Lilitri on chasing the perfect hook for six albums
sum: SPIN profiles Jade Lilitri, the songwriter behind Oso Oso, arguing he may be the best hook writer in emo right now. Lilitri jokes that he has been writing the same song across six albums, but the piece frames it as a long pursuit of the ideal version of his project.

Now 34, he talks about legacy: leaving a body of music that paints a picture of who he was, and pushing each record to its potential before Oso Oso eventually ends. He also discusses wanting listeners to feel their emotional and financial investment is respected.
pts: Six albums of big emo hooks

stories.h: Kiwi Jr. release "Something Wicked," a Blowin' Up outtake
sum: Toronto indie rockers Kiwi Jr. shared "Something Wicked," a sparkling indie-pop song cut from the Detroit sessions for their recent album Blowin' Up, which featured guests including members of Protomartyr and Alvvays.

Frontman Jeremy Gaudet says it was one of the first songs written for the record but no longer fit by the end. Its lyric riffs on Shakespeare's witches brewing up trouble. The band starts a European run on 6 November at Pitchfork Festival London.

stories.h: Hannah Jadagu returns with sleek new single "Curse"
sum: A year after her well-loved 2025 album Describe, alt-pop artist Hannah Jadagu is back with "Curse." Stereogum describes it as sleek in texture and grand in scope, with gleaming synthetic production and a magnetic vocal about wanting to understand where it hurts and what it costs.
Jadagu co-created the accompanying video with Sam Wilbert. No album has been announced yet.

stories.h: Lafa Pratomo, Jason Ranti and Isyana Sarasvati rap about AI anxiety
sum: Indonesian guitarist Lafa Pratomo released "Dogs Are Always True" on 3 November, pairing Jason Ranti and Isyana Sarasvati on an electro-pop track where both rap about fears around artificial intelligence and the noise of online life. It is the fifth release from his EP Garis Tegak.

The song grew out of Jason telling Lafa about a neighbour who lost their job to AI. The trio built it almost from scratch in jam sessions, and Isyana says it is a reminder to stay careful with unverified information online.
pts: Fifth single from EP Garis Tegak
Built from scratch in jam sessions
stories.q: Lafa Pratomo Dogs Are Always True

stories.h: mpq's Dignified Losers is about living with unfinished defeat
sum: Pophariini reviews Dignified Losers, the second album by Indonesian band mpq, reading it as a record about small, everyday defeats: work never started because it has to be perfect, tiring habits that are scarier to quit.

Opener "Not For Anyone Else" comes from Alit Djarot's struggle with overthinking and perfectionism, while closer "Miles & Miles" carries Daniel Hasudungan's view that as long as you're alive, there's still something to chase. The review frames the album as a journey from what holds you back to a reason to keep trying.
pts: Opens and closes on two outlooks

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Chopova Lowena taps Violet Grohl for its Clubhouse campaign
sum: Cult London label Chopova Lowena released a campaign starring Violet Grohl, shot by Grace Difford, celebrating its first shop: the Clubhouse at 84 Teesdale Street in East London, which opened in August with custom furniture and vintage curiosities.

At its centre is Petal, the brand's club mascot, on an exclusive line of striped tees, camo bandanas, socks, boyshorts, caps and stickers. The store also has a Skirt Bar where visitors design their own Chopova Lowena skirt from deadstock and vintage fabrics, in the brand's mix of folklore, sportswear and subculture.

stories.h: Lagos Fashion Week's street style went full colour
sum: Dazed's photo story from Lagos Fashion Week shows why the once-a-year event matters for Africa's labels and its street-style crowd. On the runway, Orange Culture returned home from Berlin with kaleidoscopic modernism, Fruché showed sculptural wooden bodices and IAMISIGO wove statuesque shapes from natural fibres.
Outside, guests went big on colour and silhouette: crimson overshirts pinned with gold brooches, chartreuse slip dresses with gold bangles and plenty of bold layering.
pts: Lagos FW happens once a year

stories.h: Denim Tears x adidas: Stan Smith and Superstar in market-bag plaid
sum: Tremaine Emory's Denim Tears has revealed its first adidas Originals collaboration: the Stan Smith and Superstar wrapped in black, blue, red and cream woven plaid taken from the Ghana Must Go market bag, with cream soles and shell toe.
A Sankofa symbol sits under co-branded tongue details. In an interview with Hypebeast, Emory explains the humble bag's place in fashion history. No release date yet.

stories.h: PUMA x JiyongKim weather the CELL Geo, out 7 November
sum: South Korean designer Jiyong Kim, known for ageing fabric with sun and the elements instead of chemical dyes, has reworked PUMA's futuristic CELL Geo with worn-in fabrics, weathered finishes, raw trims and frayed laces.

The sculptural CELL heel unit and streamlined running shape stay intact underneath. It drops globally on 7 November via PUMA, JiyongKim and select stores, with a limited Black colourway sold only by JiyongKim.

stories.h: Barbour and FARM Rio bring tropical prints to British jackets again
sum: Barbour and Brazil's FARM Rio have reunited for a third collection. FARM Rio reworks Barbour's signature tartan into two exclusive prints: one in classic browns and blues, the other bursting with florals and banana motifs.
The prints run across showerproof and quilted jackets, reversible liners, overshirts, knitwear, skirts and dresses, with floral-lined interiors and dual-branded details.
pts: Third Barbour x FARM Rio drop

stories.h: This week's drops: Supreme x Vaquera, Palace x Burberry and more
sum: Hypebeast's weekly drop roundup leads with Supreme and Vaquera's campy Fall 2026 capsule, from graphic hoodies to a duvet set. Palace marks its new Poland Street flagship in London with a store-only Burberry capsule, and BAPE and adidas push a Y2K basketball line led by the Crazy Energy+.

Also out: Crenshaw Skate Club x Sprite's barbershop-inspired streetwear, a sixth Pas Normal Studios x Salomon running capsule, and The North Face x Cecilie Bahnsen's floral-embroidered cropped Nuptse.

stories.h: Coperni shuts down after dispute with its distributor
sum: Paris label Coperni, eight years old, is closing. Founders Arnaud Vaillant and Sébastien Meyer said operating company Coperni SAS will cease trading after failing to settle a dispute over unpaid sums and licensing with distributor and shareholder Tomorrow.

Tomorrow had ended the licence amid debts, pushing Coperni into court protection earlier this year. The founders tried to buy back the brand, but governance fights, financial strain and a cancelled Fall/Winter 2026 show ended it.

stories.h: Ex-police chief Listyo Sigit named suspect in alleged wiretapping of Prabowo
sum: Former national police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo has been named a suspect, with two other police officers, in an alleged illegal wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto and other political figures, Bareskrim announced on 3 November. All three are detained at police headquarters; a fourth person remains a witness.

The case began with a 30 October report by a police officer alleging illegal interception, deletion of electronic data and illegal access. Investigators say they seized 11 phones, an iPad and four flash drives. The charges under the new Criminal Code and the ITE law carry up to 10 years in prison.
pts: Up to 10 years under new KUHP

stories.h: Civil society lists seven problems with the new Agrarian Reform Law
sum: The DPR passed the Agrarian Reform Regulation Law (UU PRA) on 22 September, but a civil-society coalition for agrarian justice says it is deeply flawed. Solidaritas Perempuan's Armayanti Sanusi told Konde.co the public still lacks access to the full text, and that drafting lacked meaningful participation.

She argues agrarian reform should correct unequal land ownership, especially for grassroots women, and that excluding farmers, Indigenous peoples, fishers and conflict-affected communities risks entrenching dominant economic interests. YLBHI's Edy Kurniawan also criticised both process and substance.

stories.h: Rain eases Central Kalimantan fires, but activists demand corporations still face the law
sum: Rain has begun to put out forest and peatland fires in Central Kalimantan after weeks of dangerous haze. Walhi Kalteng's Agung Sesa says the relief must not end law enforcement against companies suspected of involvement, and warns that El Niño continues into next year.

Mongabay reports that residents and students who protested the slow fire response were instead smeared with ethnic and religious (SARA) labels. Activists want the wet season used to prepare against repeat fires.

stories.h: Songket weavers in Pandai Sikek reject a toll road through their land
sum: In Nagari Pandai Sikek, Tanah Datar, West Sumatra, women songket weavers fear a planned toll road will take farmland, homes and ancestral pusako land. Local youth estimate it would affect 18 hectares of farmland, 1.8 hectares of housing and seven songket businesses.

Residents put farming and weaving turnover at about Rp27 billion a year. Customary leaders and residents have formally rejected the route and asked the government for an alternative; Walhi Sumbar urges respect for community land rights.

stories.h: Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim US senator
sum: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat with over 52% of the vote, beating Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim ever elected to the US Senate, Democracy Now! reports. He ran on Medicare for All, fighting inequality, getting big money out of politics and ending military aid to Israel, despite Islamophobic attacks from top Republicans.

Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in a broad rebuke of Trump. Organizer Linda Sarsour said the win shows progressives can win in states like Michigan while standing up for Palestinian rights.
pts: Ran on ending military aid to Israel

stories.h: Record number of hijab-wearing women elected in US midterms
sum: Four state senators-elect and one US congresswoman who wear the hijab won on Tuesday, a national record, Middle East Eye reports, despite surging anti-Muslim rhetoric since Trump returned to power in January 2025.
Among them is Georgia's Ruwa Romman. The Muslim Public Affairs Council had warned that far-right provocations might deter Muslim voters, but several young, visibly Muslim women rose to office anyway.

stories.h: Gaza mission surgeon Adam Hamawy wins a House seat in New Jersey
sum: Egyptian-American surgeon Adam Hamawy, who did medical missions in Gaza, won New Jersey's 12th congressional district, becoming the first Muslim and first Egyptian American to represent the state in the House, Middle East Eye reports.
In his victory speech he addressed the people of Gaza directly and vowed to hold Trump accountable. His win is part of a Democratic wave projected to give the party around 250 House seats.
pts: First Muslim House rep from NJ
Spoke to Gaza in victory speech

stories.h: Over 1,100 child amputees in Gaza blocked from treatment abroad, NGO says
sum: The Geneva-based Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor says 1,134 children in Gaza have lost limbs in Israeli attacks, and that Israeli limits on travel and medical evacuations keep most from specialised care abroad, Al Jazeera reports.

The WHO says of 2,300 amputees assessed between September 2024 and May 2026, only about 500 received permanent prosthetics. Euro-Med says just eight certified prosthetics professionals work in Gaza, warning unadjusted limbs could cause lifelong pain as children grow.

stories.h: UNRWA mass layoffs in Gaza seen as an attack on refugee rights
sum: UNRWA has dismissed hundreds of staff in Gaza, citing a $70 million shortfall, and its acting chief told the staff union he plans to end thousands of contracts across the region. Mondoweiss spoke to laid-off workers like a microfinance officer of 13 years who is now broke.

Staff, the union and a former spokesperson say the cuts target the refugee question itself, since UNRWA embodies Palestinians' claim to return after the Nakba. The layoffs come as the US-led Board of Peace prepares to oversee Gaza's post-war governance.
pts: Union: cuts target right of return

stories.h: Palestine Action ban challenged at UK Supreme Court; dozens arrested outside
sum: The campaign to overturn the UK's terrorism designation of Palestine Action reached the Supreme Court in a two-day hearing, while dozens were arrested outside, Middle East Eye reports.

Representing co-founder Huda Ammori, Raza Husain KC argued that under 1% of the group's protests met the legal definition of terrorism and that it never advocated violence against people, comparing its tactics to the Suffragettes and other movements never proscribed.
